CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidney stones

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male presenting for evaluation of right-sided kidney stone. Approximately one week ago, patient developed sudden onset right-sided back pain while working in a barn moving hay. He initially attributed the pain to the physical activity but developed associated diaphoresis and nausea. Pain radiated nearly to the groin. He presented to his PCP who ordered a CT scan confirming the presence of a kidney stone. Since the initial episode, pain has recurred intermittently but with shorter duration and lower intensity. Patient denies current severe pain. He has been straining his urine as instructed and reports no visible stones in the strainer. Denies hematuria or dark-colored urine. This is his first episode of kidney stones. He notes his father has a history of recurrent kidney stones.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for diaphoresis and nausea at time of initial pain onset. Denies fever, hematuria, or dark urine. Reports intermittent pain that has improved in frequency and duration.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No prior kidney stones

MEDICATIONS
Patient reports taking Tylenol

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Father with history of recurrent kidney stones

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works with horses on a farm, performing manual labor including moving hay

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs stable, no fever. Blood pressure and heart rate normal. Abdominal examination reveals no tenderness to palpation, no rebound tenderness, and no guarding. Costovertebral angle (CVA) tenderness present on right side.

RESULTS
CT scan demonstrates a kidney stone measuring 0.5 cm located in the proximal right ureter. No hydronephrosis identified. Pending results: BMP, urinalysis, and urine culture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right-sided kidney stone, proximal right ureter, 0.5 cm, without obstruction. Patient counseled to increase fluid intake to facilitate urine production and stone passage. Prescribed oxycodone 5 mg every 6 to 8 hours for pain management with acetaminophen available for breakthrough pain. Patient to continue straining urine. Labs ordered including BMP, urinalysis, and urine culture to assess for infection and guide need for antibiotic therapy. Follow-up appointment in 1 to 2 weeks. If stone has not passed by follow-up visit, further discussion regarding lithotripsy will be undertaken.
